description: From the free upper park of the Cornisa, Cartagena's Roman theatre lies below in the haze — the cavea curving where 7,000 spectators once sat, discovered only in 1987 beneath the old cathedral. On a foggy 21°C night the ancient tiers glow softly in moonlight while the harbor's lights shimmer beyond. It's the view locals say beats even the paid visit: two thousand years of stone, free from above.
